episodes.213890: Initial shower and thunderstorm coverage during the morning hours of July 18, 2026 moved east of the region and allowed for ample recovery with respect to instability across the region during the late morning and early afternoon hours. The remnants of a MCS that tracked across Ohio and western Pennsylvania continued into northern Somerset County during the morning hours and produced multiple instances of tree damage as it continued into northern Bedford County in the early afternoon hours. At the same time, thunderstorm development across northwestern Pennsylvania began to rapidly show upscale growth within a strongly sheared and unstable environment, allowing for multiple instances of tree damage in Warren County. Storms began to quickly show signs of rotation as they moved further southeast into Elk County and produced wind damage, but no convergent patterns in damage were found. As these storms continues southeastward with continued rotation, a tornado occurred in northern Centre County and multiple instances of tree damage were observed in Clinton County. In the late afternoon hours, additional rotating cells came from western Pennsylvania, spawning an EF-2 tornado in Somerset County where widespread tree damage was observed. These cells also spawned three tornadoes, with an EF-1 in Clearfield County, an EF-2 in Huntingdon County, and an EF-0 in Blair County. Wind damage continues to be observed from these storms through the Lower Susquehanna Valley, mainly in the form of tree damage. Multiple rounds of storms in Clearfield and Somerset Counties also resulted in isolated instances of flash flooding on roadways.
episodes.213898: A plume of monsoon moisture between an upper low over the Permian Basin of western Texas and southeast New Mexico and a disturbance over Arizona resulted in diurnal shower and thunderstorm activity first across the higher terrain before moving south and west into nearby highlands and valley locations. Thunderstorms producing locally heavy rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches resulted in flash flooding in Gallup and Zuni Pueblo during the evening hours of July 16th. Heavy rainfall amounts of up to 2 inches on the South Fork burn scar just west of Ruidoso on July 17th resulted in flash flooding and debris flows on and downstream of the Cedar Creek area. A low water crossing flooded from heavy rains in northwestern Roswell on the 18th, while storms producing flash flooding impacted areas just northeast of Grants, NM on the 19th.
episodes.213971: On the afternoon of July 17, a thunderstorm moved southward from Walker County into Jefferson County, producing a few instances of minor tree damage around Empire and Bagley. Also associated with this thunderstorm, numerous photos and videos were taken of a funnel-like cloud. One video showed what appeared to be a very brief and small condensation funnel in an open field behind homes on Daniel Trail. This funnel produced no damage and was determined to be a brief gustnado occurring under the shelf cloud of the larger thunderstorm.||More afternoon thunderstorms on July 18 and 19 produced minor tree damage across a few counties.
episodes.214070: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours of July 19, 2026. An abundant amount of atmospheric moisture allowed these thunderstorms to produce another round of heavy rain. The most significant flooding was reported in southern Lawrence County and Cookeville where several area roadways were reported flooded and impassable.
episodes.214254: A slow moving upper level low lingered over the area during the day on the 18th which resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms across the entire region. Strong heating during the afternoon provided the necessary instability for thunderstorm development. Wind shear was weak so thunderstorms struggled to become organized but a few were able to produce severe wind gusts. One landspout was observed near Lorenzo that remained over open fields. Additionally, the lack of wind shear led to slow movement of storms which produced localized heavy rainfall. Minor flooding was reported in the town of Matador (Motley County).
episodes.214714: An upper-level trough maintained its position over west Texas and southeast New Mexico on the 18th, interacting with ample moisture across the region. As a result, showers and thunderstorms once again developed across the area. Slow storm motion and heavy rainfall led to flash flooding for numerous locations in the Permian Basin and in southeast New Mexico.
episodes.214715: An upper-level trough maintained its position over west Texas and southeast New Mexico on the 18th, interacting with ample moisture across the region. As a result, showers and thunderstorms once again developed across the area. Slow storm motion and heavy rainfall led to flash flooding for numerous locations in the Permian Basin and in southeast New Mexico.
episodes.214716: Some continued lift from a weakening trough (coupled with upslope flow) led to shower and thunderstorm development again on the 19th across portions of west Texas and southeast New Mexico (with the greatest concentration around the higher terrain by the afternoon). Flash flooding of streets and creeks was reported in Alpine.
episodes.214952: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced several wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.215516: A stalled frontal boundary bisected Eastern North Carolina through the overnight hours on July nineteenth. This front combined with the sea breeze and ample instability to promote the development of thunderstorm clusters during the afternoon and evening hours on July nineteenth. A few of these storms became strong to severe in nature bringing damaging wind gusts and even a report of a waterspout to areas along and north of the Neuse River.
episodes.215942: A tropical upper tropospheric trough (TUTT) across south Florida on July 16th shifted northwestward and closed off into an upper low over the northeastern Gulf on July 17th. The combination of deep tropical moisture and mid level cooler air overspread into northern Florida and Georgia supporting numerous showers and thunderstorms each afternoon and evening developing along the inland-moving sea breezes. A broad surface low then developed under the upper low in the northeastern Gulf and gradually deepened into Invest 91 on July 18th and then strengthened into Tropical Depression 2 on July 19th. Showers and thunderstorms rotated around the eastern side of the system shifting northward up the Florida peninsula July 19th into July 20th. A few strong to severe storms developed as the outer rainbands from TD 2 interacted with the sea breeze and outflow boundaries. On July 20th, mid-level drier air filtered into the area from the south triggering some stronger downbursts.
episodes.215958: A monsoonal pattern persisted onward through mid July, resulting in more instances of thunderstorm winds and flash flooding.
episodes.215988: Despite nebulous synoptic and mesoscale forcing, scattered diurnal thunderstorms developed across portions of southern Oklahoma and western-north Texas on the 19th. A briefly severe thunderstorm produced observations of severe winds near Seymour, TX.
episodes.216186: A trough across the southern Appalachians led to the development of scattered showers and storms across the central and northern Piedmont. Several trees were reported down across Granville, Durham, Vance, and Johnston Counties.
episodes.216187: A southward moving cold front from the Middle Atlantic region produced showers and storms across central North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening hours. Storms started across the northern Piedmont and Coastal Plain, eventually shifting into the southern Piedmont and Sandhills during the late evening and early overnight hours.
episodes.216297: Isolated strong thunderstorms produced high winds in central and north central South Dakota during the evening of July 19. ||In Campbell County, the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station two miles north of Herreid measured an extreme wind gust of 87 mph. The same storm system previously struck Mobridge, where the Mobridge Regional Airport ASOS recorded a 64 mph (56 knots) gust, downing tree branches and damaging the screen support structures at the Mobridge Pheasant Drive-In.||In central South Dakota, thunderstorm wind gusts of 62 mph were recorded on a public mesonet station near Presho and the South Dakota State University mesonet station 6 miles south southeast of Kennebec in central South Dakota.
episodes.216341: An upper level shortwave moved over a very hot and humid airmass, leading to scattered thunderstorms developing along a surface trough in central North Dakota. The main threat with these supercell thunderstorms was large hail, with the largest hail of 2 inches in diameter reported south of Dawson in Kidder County. There were also a few reports of damaging thunderstorm wind gusts as the storms moved east into south central North Dakota and the southern James River Valley. The strongest reported wind gust was 72 mph at the NDAWN station near Wirch in McIntosh County.
episodes.216399: Widespread, diurnally forced thunderstorms, developed during the afternoon of July 19th across much of East Tennessee and southwest Virginia. These storms produced some isolated flash flooding in the Tennessee valley and also in parts of southwest Virginia.
episodes.216400: Widespread, diurnally forced thunderstorms, developed during the afternoon of July 19th across much of East Tennessee and southwest Virginia. These storms produced some isolated flash flooding in the Tennessee valley and also in parts of southwest Virginia.
episodes.216512: Thunderstorms quickly developed in the late afternoon hours along and ahead of an approaching cold front. High dew points in the low 70s with upper 70s air temperatures were supportive of 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE and 30-40 knots of effective shear, plenty for storm organization. Storms congealed and moved southeast through the area in broken line segments producing swaths of wind damage and a couple embedded tornadoes. Training of storms lead to isolated instances of flash flooding as well.
episodes.216523: The region was along the edge of an area of high pressure from the 16th-18th. This positioning kept feeding in monsoonal moisture and instability to produce daily severe isolated severe thunderstorms to the region.
episodes.216587: Broad cyclonic flow aloft over the eastern Gulf and Florida peninsula coupled with a developing surface low over the eastern Gulf that would become Tropical Storm Bertha created a favorable convective environment that produced waterspouts near Punta Rassa and Bradenton Beach, and strong marine wind gusts over the Tampa Bay waters.
episodes.216733: An upper high was located over Colorado with northeast flow over southern New Mexico. Residual monsoonal moisture was still in the area and allowed for heavy rain and flash flooding to occur around Las Cruces and a severe thunderstorm moved through the Lordsburg Playa.
episodes.216771: Moisture lingered over southern New Mexico as an upper high became situated over Colorado.  A weak upper trough moved through Texas and helped to support slow moving thunderstorms with heavy rain and some severe wind gusts over Dona Ana and Grant counties.
episodes.216904: An isolated thunderstorm produced a severe wind gust near Haskell.
episodes.216929: Thunderstorms developed across southwest Alabama and produced gusty winds.
episodes.217080: Monsoon moisture fueled thunderstorms with heavy rain across Mohave County.
episodes.217102: Another multiple day period of unsettled weather occurred between July 17th and 19th across the Ohio Valley. On July 17th, the synoptic pattern featured weak flow through much of the troposphere, with the region being on the eastern side of an expansive upper ridge. However, hot and humid conditions were present, allowing for between 2000 and 3000 J/kg of mixed-layer CAPE to develop across central Kentucky during the afternoon hours. Given the weak flow aloft, pulse convection was mainly experienced across the area, although a few stronger storm cores were able to produce downbursts resulting in isolated wind damage. Later in the evening, a cluster of storms across south central Kentucky congealed into a large mass of heavy rainfall, with precipitable water values exceeding 2 inches and decreasing instability allowing for efficient rainfall production. This resulted in isolated instances of flash flooding near Green River Lake. On the 18th, an approaching cold front and mid-level trough helped to increase the wind shear and forcing for storms, with more organized convection developing during the afternoon and evening hours. The strongest storm of the day went across the southwest side of the Louisville metro, producing several instances of wind damage. Finally, as the cold front sank to the south during the afternoon on July 19th, training thunderstorms in a rich moisture environment once again produced isolated flash flooding, this time in Cumberland and Clinton County.

An EF-1 tornado with estimated peak winds of 110 mph, a path length of 1 mile, and a maximum width of 400 yards occurred near Houtzdale on July 18, 2026. Tree damage first began near the northwestern end of Gum Street and continued southeastward towards PA-153. Several pine trees were snapped and minor damage was noted to structures along Hemlock Street. The tornado continued to produce extensive damage to trees and power lines as it moved across North Railroad Street. A chimney was ripped off of a house on Hale Road along with additional damage to trees in this area. Hundreds of trees were uprooted or snapped as the tornado continued along its path before the tornado briefly lifted as it crossed an open field. Damage resumed as the tornado moved back into a forested area along Hale Road toward Sonia Lane. Extensive damage to trees and powerlines was noted in this area. Damage then became much more sporadic as the circulation crossed Moshannon Creek, where the tornado path ended.

An EF-2 tornado with estimated peak winds of 125 mph, a path length of 0.53 miles, and a maximum path width of 500 yards occurred along Old Mill Road in Franklin Township on July 18, 2026. Minor damage was first noted near Huntingdon Furnace Road where a few corn stalks were knocked down. The first structural damage was observed as the roof of a silo was partially blown off. Half of a barn roof was also blown off and a nearby barn lost several pieces of its roof. The tornado continued southeast, paralleling Warriors Mark Run and Old Mill Road where it produced significant damage to trees. Hundreds of trees were snapped or uprooted along the path. One tree fell onto a cabin with two people inside, though they were uninjured as they were safely sheltered on the opposite side of the cabin. The tornado continued east-southeastward towards Camp Kanesatake and ended as it crossed Old Mill Road on the north edge of the camp. Sporadic tree damage was noted downstream of the camp, but this was likely due to straight-line winds.

A significant debris flow and flash flood wave was reported by multiple sources, including cameras deployed by emergency management, broadcast media, public, department of transportation, and various other law enforcement agencies. There was widespread flooding through the Grove area of Beaver. Media reports showed multiple homes were impacted by flood waters, including carried rocks and logs, causing significant damage to outbuildings, some of which were destroyed or swept downstream. For a period of time, helicopter rescues from rooftops were required. A diversion dam structure in the canyon was completely removed by the flood waters, and an early warning flood camera mounted many feet above the river was removed as well. Beaver County issued a Go Status evacuation to all residence within 1/4 mile of the Beaver River and North Creek. The water supply to the town of Beaver was been compromised by flood waters and residences are under a boil water notice. Interstate 15 was closed in both direction at the Beaver River for approximately 6 hours as  the debris flow and flash flood waters breached the interstate. A Flash Flood Emergency was issued for this event.
